_comment: Fusion parameters. Data, not code, so eval_fusion.py can tune them
and the report can cite the exact values a result was produced with.
per_class_f1 entries are the measured per-class F1 of each modality
on its own test set. They are normalised to mean 1.0 at load time,
so what matters is the ratio between classes within a modality, not
the absolute scale.
base_weight: relative trust in each modality overall, tuned by eval_fusion.py --tune against a mismatch mix of 0/10/20/35%. Face is below text because it measures materially weaker cross-dataset.

face.source: vit-emotion-v4, deployed configuration (aligned crop, multi-crop ensemble, T+logit_bias), measured on eval_data_unseen/test/webcam - a split held out from BOTH training and calibration fitting. The calibration was fitted on eval_data_unseen/calib/webcam, a disjoint set of images. Earlier versions of these numbers were measured on rows the calibration had been fitted on.
face._note: v4 on the untouched test split: 52.3% accuracy, 49.7% macro-F1, 44.4% neutral F1, against v3 48.0/46.9/38.6 and v2 32.9/32.5/19.4 on the same images. disgust stays low (0.20) and is left unsmoothed so fusion distrusts it.

_comment: The earlier values were measured before three deployment bugs
were fixed, so they described a pipeline that no longer runs:
the crop was ~5x tighter than training framing, the stored
temperature was below 1.0 and therefore sharpened rather than
softened, and no logit_bias was applied. The neutral entry is
the one that moved least in absolute terms but mattered most:
under the old pipeline the model emitted 'neutral' on 2 of 693
unseen faces, so its 0.3687 was not reproducible at all.
Keeping them here because fusion weights are tuned against
these ratios and the change should be auditable.

text._note: per_class_f1 from the GoEmotions test split (4968 rows), TinyBERT.

_comment: text_half_life_seconds: how long until a message counts for half.
Face evidence is continuous and text arrives in bursts, so without
decay a single old message would pin the fused label forever.
30s is roughly conversational turn scale.
text_cutoff_seconds: past this the message contributes nothing at
all, so a stale session collapses cleanly to face-only rather than
trailing an ever-smaller but nonzero term.

low_agreement_threshold: Bhattacharyya coefficient below which two differing predictions count as a conflict. 0.80 rather than something near 0 because over 7 classes the shared tails floor the coefficient around 0.4 even for fully opposed peaked distributions - see the measured table in fusion.agreement().
